title: Randomized product noise identity
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $c\in\mathbb R$, let $f$ be real-valued on its outcome space, and choose $r\in\{0,1\}^n$. Define coordinate rates $s_i=c$ when $r_i=0$ and $s_i=-c$ when $r_i=1$. As functions on the outcome space, randomizing the product noise of $f$ at rate $c$ gives the anisotropic product noise with rates $s_i$: $R_r(T_cf)=T_{\boldsymbol{s}}f$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is a real-valued function on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $c\in\mathbb R$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $r\in\{0,1\}^n$. Then $R_r(T_cf)=T_{\boldsymbol s}f$ for $s_i=c(-1)^{r_i}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$; $R_rh=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\chi_S(r)h_S$; $T_{\boldsymbol s}h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}(\prod_{i\in S}s_i)h_S$ for real coordinate rates $s_i$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
